title: Outreach Kaia Alternatives in 2026
summary: Six honest Outreach Kaia alternatives for 2026, from Clari Copilot to Salesloft, with a comparison table and the real reasons teams look beyond Kaia.
body_markdown:
Most teams searching for Outreach Kaia alternatives are not unhappy with Kaia itself. They have hit one of its boundaries: they do not run Outreach, they need answers Kaia's pre-built cards cannot give, or they want help on meetings Outreach never booked.


## 01


What does Outreach Kaia do well?


Outreach Kaia is the AI meeting assistant built into the Outreach sales execution platform. It joins meetings booked through Outreach, transcribes them live, surfaces content cards when the conversation hits a trigger your enablement team set, captures action items as they come up, and writes the summary back into Outreach when the call ends.


For a team that runs Outreach end to end, that is hard to beat on friction. There is no extra vendor, no separate note-taker in the meeting, and no copy-paste step afterwards. The rep sees a card the moment a competitor comes up, and the record lands next to the sequences and deals the team already works in. If that describes your team, and Kaia's cards cover the questions your buyers ask, you may not need an alternative at all.


## 02


Why do teams look for Outreach Kaia alternatives?


Three reasons come up again and again, and none of them is that Kaia does its job badly.


**You do not run Outreach.** Kaia is a feature of the platform, with no standalone version. If your team is on Salesloft, HubSpot, or a homegrown stack, adopting Kaia means adopting Outreach, and that is a platform decision, not a meeting-assistant decision.


**Cards only answer the questions someone predicted.** Kaia's content cards surface material your team wrote in advance and must keep current. When a buyer asks something outside the deck (a niche integration, a security detail, how you differ from a rival on one feature) the card for it may simply not exist. Teams that want an answer built from their own docs, CRM notes, and past calls need a different engine.


**Help stops at the edge of Outreach meetings.** Kaia assists meetings booked through Outreach. Inbound calls, ad hoc conversations, and calls that run through a separate dialler fall outside its reach.


If any of these sound familiar, our roundup of[real-time AI sales assistants by use case](https://www.caretta.so/blog/best-real-time-ai-sales-assistants) pairs well with the list below.


## 03


What are the best Outreach Kaia alternatives?


Six established options, judged on the three gaps above. No obscure startups, no padding.


### 1. Caretta


The strongest match for the second and third gaps. It listens to the live call and generates answers from your organisation's own knowledge: docs, CRM, past calls, and the way your best reps handle the same question. So when a buyer asks something no one wrote a card for, the rep still gets a usable answer while the buyer is on the line. It also briefs the rep before the call and drafts notes and follow-ups after it, and it does not care which platform booked the meeting. Honest limit: it has no sequences or dialler of its own, so most teams run it alongside Outreach or Salesloft. See[how it draws on your own content](https://www.caretta.so/product) .


### 2. Clari Copilot


The closest like-for-like if your only blocker is the Outreach dependency. Clari Copilot shows battlecards during the call when it hears a trigger you set, nudges reps on monologues and talk ratio, and scores calls afterwards. It sits inside Clari's revenue platform, so it fits best if your forecasting lives there. The model is the same as Kaia's: someone on your team writes the cards and keeps them current, and questions outside the cards go unanswered.


### 3. Gong


The category leader in conversation intelligence, and a post-call tool. Be clear-eyed about that: Gong records and analyses calls after they end, then produces scorecards, deal warnings, and forecasts. Nothing appears in front of the rep mid-call. As a replacement for Kaia's capture and summary side, it is far deeper than Kaia. As a replacement for the live cards, it is the wrong tool. If live coaching is your axis, we compare the options in[Gong alternatives for real-time coaching](https://www.caretta.so/blog/gong-alternatives-real-time-coaching) .


### 4. Avoma


A meeting lifecycle assistant: agenda templates before the meeting, transcription and collaborative notes during it, conversation intelligence and scorecards after it. It works across the common meeting and CRM stacks and tends to suit smaller budgets than the platform vendors. Live assistance is thin, so treat it as a capture and analytics choice.


### 5. Dialpad


If your calls run through Dialpad's dialler, its real-time assist cards behave much like Kaia's: a trigger phrase brings up the content your team loaded, and managers can watch live transcripts and coach mid-call. The boundary is the dialler itself. Calls and meetings outside Dialpad get nothing, so it fits phone-heavy inbound and outbound teams best.


### 6. Salesloft


The platform-parallel option. If the honest question behind your search is whether to run Outreach at all, Salesloft is the other major sales engagement platform, with its own conversation intelligence for recording and analysing calls built in. Choosing it is a stack decision on the same scale as choosing Outreach. Its conversation tools lean post-call, so teams that want live prompts usually still add a real-time assistant on top.


## 04


How do the alternatives compare?


Tool Live help in the call Where answers come from Buy without Outreach?


Outreach Kaia Yes: content cards, live transcription Cards your team writes No, part of Outreach


Caretta Yes: generated answers Your docs, CRM, and past calls Yes


Clari Copilot Yes: triggered battlecards Cards your team writes Yes


Gong No, post-call analysis Its analysis of your recordings Yes


Avoma Limited Notes and analytics from your meetings Yes


Dialpad Yes, on dialler calls Cards your team writes Yes


Salesloft Mostly post-call Its analysis of your recordings Yes


## 05


How should you choose?


Match the tool to the gap that sent you looking. If you love Kaia's model but do not run Outreach, Clari Copilot gives you the same card-based coaching without the platform commitment, and Dialpad does the same for dialler-based teams. If your gap is that cards cannot answer unpredicted questions, pick the generated-answer route at the top of the list. If what you actually valued was the capture and the summaries, Gong and Avoma do that side better than Kaia ever aimed to.


And if you run Outreach happily and buyers rarely surprise your reps, keep Kaia. The lowest-friction tool you already own beats a better tool nobody adopts.
